notes: **Statement 008-N1.** The author proposes placing disjunction–compatibility axioms before the axioms on lieux, so as not to appear to make them depend on the latter. They are called “facultatifs” for an atelier, with mutual implications anticipated. The page then defines disjointness by compatibility and empty intersection and states its stratum formulation (Grothendieck, 1986, scan8).

**Statement 008-N2 — stratum equivalence checked by R2 and rechecked by M.** Assume the earlier representation by nonempty strata, the bottom empty figure and hereditary compatibility. If F and G are disjoint, each pair of their strata is compatible and cannot have a common lower stratum, since that stratum would lie below F∩G. Conversely, pairwise disjoint strata give pairwise compatibility and hence F compatible G by At3. A nonempty intersection would contain a stratum Z by the earlier generation property, and the pair Z,Z would contradict the assumed disjointness. This checks the displayed equivalence under those stated earlier axioms; it does not prove a spaciousness assertion.

**Statement 008-N3 — conditional check of the NB forward implication.** M, R2 and R3 independently checked the following bounded argument, conditional on the minimal/minimum interpretation of the uncertain AtM4(a) adjective on007. If X and Y are compatible and Z≪X,Z≪Y, choose minimal A≤X and B≤Y in the respective selected fibres. Their minimality also holds in their own lower fibres, so Z circle-refines A and B. Downward compatibility gives A compatible B; AtM4(b) gives A=B. Hence there is a common lower stratum, contradicting X∥Y. This verifies the stated forward implication under the explicit minimality interpretation. An arbitrary privileged element would not justify the same argument, and the proof does not settle that earlier word.

**Statement 008-N4 — limited reverse implication.** AtM0 says ≤ implies ≪. Therefore a common ≤-lower stratum would also be a common ≪-refiner. Absence of a common refiner excludes a common lower stratum, but does not by this argument establish compatibility. The latter is also required for X∥Y. R2 and R3 checked this limited implication; M rechecked it. The author attributes a fuller reciprocal assertion to an axiom below; that promise is preserved without treating the compatibility component as proved.

**Statement 008-N5 — cancelled draft.** The lower At DC1 and Cor propose compatibility tests involving refinements disjoint from the intersection K. The inserted NB says “et alors seulement…” and refers to Cor; the left margin names the condition and gives “les ateliers simpliciaux” as counterexamples. The whole lower draft is crossed by three long diagonals; one also crosses the marginal paragraph. No proof of the proposed axiom, its converse, the corollary or the counterexample class was attempted. Those are manuscript assertions carried as background.

**Reading decisions.** Both interlinear guides are drawn. The NB verb has one shared stem with an overwritten ending, not two complete written verbs. Its earlier and current suffixes remain doubtful. A possible clipped closing parenthesis after Z≪Y is retained against both witnesses’ comma, without repairing the resulting punctuation. The guide-like mark before K is drawn as the primary alternative to deleted et. Both occurrences of spacieux/specieux remain unaccented a/e doubts. The Cor first live index is plain F, while the second carries a separate tilde; mathematical expectation does not supply a missing decoration. The oval has ses and a small upper-right gap.

**Source and scope limits.** R1 reports that C’s audit paragraph headed Scan8 discusses a different NB margin; material absent from this image was not imported. The directly matching C page and all21 in-place doubts were audited. H’s emphasis macro represents authorial emphasis, so same-span emphasis conversions alone are not counted. Manuscript page7 is written at the top; no new date, title sheet or page count occurs here. No later manuscript page or external source was consulted before this gate.
